Like the victims of those enslaved warriors, I felt pummelled by the experience.
School of Rock lacks for some of the mayhem of Matilda, the dash of Spring Awakening, the pathos of Billy Elliot.

And that means that despite the contributions of its famous composer, Andrew Lloyd Webber, “School of Rock” has to settle for reduced status as another formulaic attempt by Broadway to capitalize on a popular movie of fairly recent vintage.
Broadway musicals can still surprise, delight, and rock out with the best of them
School of Rock is a big, beautiful blast of musical comedy from start to finish.
School of Rock – The Musical is full of both hard-charging rock n roll and supremely catchy melodies.
School of Rock isn't perfect. But if, as the musical suggests, perfection is less the point than trying hard and having fun doing so, then it succeeds.

Essentially a modern version of 'The Music Man,' it charts how out-of-work musician Dewey Finn (Alex Brightman) lands a gig as a substitute teacher at a snobby prep school and turns his class into a garage band, giving the children self-confidence in the process...The dozen or so children are wildly talented and absolutely adorable.

Andrew Lloyd Webber's first new work for Broadway in a decade is an otherwise workaday screen-to-stage adaptation, with a generous (and, I'm guessing, hoarse after every show) lead actor and faithful, if prosaic book by an unlikely writer-'Downton Abbey' creator Julian Fellowes.
